results.reason: Item 1 identifies SA §2.2 automatic five-year Renewal Terms, the 270/240-day notice window, calls it effectively a 30-day window, and explains that missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Item 3 quotes 'all glass and PET containers... worldwide' and contrasts this with the Term Sheet's amber glass bottles for beer brands at U.S./Canadian facilities. It states Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.

Item 2 cites Recital C, receipt on August 3, 2026, and expiry on September 2, 2026, 19 days before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted absent an extension or waiver.

The response never addresses Amendment Section 2's replacement of SA §11.2. It does not mention the removal of recall costs from the cap carve-outs or the narrowing of the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims.

Item 4 identifies new §14.4 under Amendment §4, which allows assignment without Customer consent to Affiliates or successors and overrides §14.3. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that the restriction is now one-sided.
The response states that under SA §15.2 written amendments rank first, and that where the Amendment conflicts with the SA, the Amendment controls.
The response states that SA §11.1 caps liability at the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner, with numbered items. Each item has a Location and a Recommended fix.
The response provides proposed language for a revised renewal clause, a narrowed §3.1, and a competitor exclusion for assignment.
The response states the window has closed and the increase is deemed accepted. It advises against telling the client it can still object.
The response states the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded, and that it would not advise that the narrower scope governs.
